thread:
alexp: quick run update — did a 60s nsys capture on the staging runner with kv_cache=on, batch=8, seq=1024. main goal: confirm kernel ranking after the recent kv-prefetch change.

mira: nice, which commit? did you reproduce the perf regression from last week?

alexp: checkout `serving/runtime:feat/kv-prefetch-v2` at d3f4a2. earlier pprof showed ~12% tail latency jump. aiming to find top time sinks.

sam_k: please dump the top kernels by total_time and by SM_occupancy — those two can diverge a lot for attention kernels.

alexp: pasted the top-10 by total GPU time (nsys summary):
```
1) fused_attn_forward  — 38.2% total_time
2) aten::matmul         — 21.7%
3) kv_prefetch_kernel   — 9.8%
4) cudaMemcpyAsync      — 7.1%
5) softmax_kernel       — 5.4%
6) layernorm_forward    — 4.0%
7) quant_dequant_kernel — 3.0%
8) aten::add            — 2.1%
9) rocm_sync_stub       — 1.5%
10) debug_fill          — 1.2%
```

neal: kv_prefetch at 9.8% is higher than I expected. is that pure compute or memory bound? what about stall stats?

alexp: nsys timeline + per-kernel metrics show kv_prefetch is very high in L2 requests and has low achieved occupancy (~28%) with high warp_stall_memory_dependency. suggests it's memory-bound and suffers from bank contention.

mira: interesting — the new prefetch path does more scatter loads. could be thrashing L2 with small irregular accesses. any difference with batch=1?

alexp: ran batch=1 quickly — kv_prefetch drops to ~3.4% total_time and its occupancy improves slightly, but overall token throughput drops. points to prefetch being amortized across batch in a weird way.

jen: can you share the nsys cmd you used? I want to repro locally.

alexp: sure:
```
nsys profile --sample=none -o /tmp/kvrun --trace=cuda,osrt --force-overwrite --duration=60s \
  --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-end=stop --cpuctx-switched-off --stats=true \
  -- python -m serving.bench --cfg=staging --batch=8 --seq=1024
```

tracebot: automated note: uploaded /artifacts/nsys/1718531234-kvrun.qdrep (60s)

sam_k: good. next step: collect per-kernel memory metrics (gputrace) and run a microprobe of kv_prefetch to see memory access pattern. also try increasing prefetch stride coalescing.

mira: also try enabling L2 caching hints and split prefetch into two phases: head prefetch (dense) + fallback scatter (sparse). that reduced stalls in my sim last month.

alexp: +1. I also noticed fused_attn_forward dominates — 38% is big. nvprof flame showed a big chunk in softmax and matmul path inside fused kernel. might be worth experimenting with kernel tiling or splitting fused into two kernels for long sequences.

neal: before splitting, try kernel launch parameter sweep. sometimes occupancy low because block size is off for seq=1024. run quick param scan varying block_x in {64,128,256} and shared mem config.

jen: for the sweep, I recommend this helper script snippet (quick):
```
for bs in 64 128 256; do 
  export KERNEL_BLOCK_X=$bs
  python -m serving.bench --batch=8 --seq=1024 --warm=5 --iter=20 > /tmp/sweep_$bs.log &
  sleep 1
done
```

alexp: will run that today. also adding perfetto trace to capture CPU/GPU interaction; some of the memcpy spikes align with scheduler backpressure from the runtime.

mira: can you check KV cache eviction rate during the run? if prefetch is launching too early we may be evicting hot entries and reloading them which can amplify memory churn.

alexp: checked eviction logs — eviction rate increased ~30% in batch=8 vs batch=1 after the change. suspect prefetch window is too large for our cache size.

sam_k: two quick experiments to prioritize: (1) reduce prefetch depth by half and re-run nsys; (2) run fused_attn with tuned block sizes. whichever reduces top-1 kernel time more gets the canary.

neal: add a metric to the rollouts dashboard: ratio of kv_prefetch_time / total_gpu_time and eviction_rate — that'll help gating.

jen: can somebody create a short PR that adds the prefetch depth config to runtime flags and default to old value? we should be able to revert quickly if the canary fails.

alexp: opening PR now with benchmark notes and nsys artifact link. I'll post results as soon as sweeps finish. :thumbsup:

mira: thanks — keep the thread updated. small wins here will cut 10-15% token cost if we avoid unnecessary mem churn.

tracebot: reminder: set nsys artifact retention=14d for these traces

alexp: noted. will ping when done.
